title: Alert
description: Alerts provide important information and feedback to users about system states, user actions, or potential issues. They appear prominently to capture attention while remaining contextually appropriate.
content: # Alert Alerts communicate important information to users in a prominent, contextually appropriate way. The ELEVATE Alert component helps designers and developers create consistent feedback systems that enhance user understanding while maintaining interface harmony. ## Overview ### When to Use Alerts - **System feedback**: Confirm successful actions, warn about potential issues, or report errors - **Important announcements**: Notify users about system updates, maintenance, or feature changes - **Contextual guidance**: Provide helpful information or tips related to current user tasks - **Status updates**: Communicate the current state of processes, applications, or user accounts - **Validation messages**: Display form validation results, input requirements, or submission status ### When NOT to Use Alerts - **Toast notifications**: Use Toast component for temporary, dismissible messages - **Inline validation**: Use field-level validation for immediate input feedback - **Loading states**:

title: Application
description: Root application wrapper component that provides theme context, global styles, and foundational setup for ELEVATE applications
content: # Application The Application component serves as the root wrapper for ELEVATE applications, providing essential setup including theme context, global styles, CSS custom properties, and foundational configuration. ## When to Use - **Root Component**: Wrap your entire application at the top level - **Theme Setup**: Enable ELEVATE theming and design tokens - **Global Styles**: Apply ELEVATE global styles and CSS reset - **Context Providers**: Initialize ELEVATE context providers ## Basic Usage ## Theme Integration ## Properties | Property | Type | Default | Description | |----------|------|---------|-------------| | `theme` | `'light' \| 'dark' \| 'auto'` | `'auto'` | Sets the application theme mode | | `compact` | `boolean` | `false` | Enables compact spacing mode | | `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | `'ltr'` | Sets text direction for internationalization | ## Slots | Slot | Description | |------|-------------| | Default | Main application content | ## Framework Integration ### React Usage ###

title: Avatar
description: Avatars represent users or entities with profile images, initials, or icons. They provide visual identification in interfaces and support various sizes and states.
content: # Avatar Avatars are visual representations of users, teams, or entities within interfaces. The ELEVATE Avatar component helps designers and developers create consistent, accessible identity systems that enhance user recognition and provide clear visual identification across all interface contexts. ## Overview ### When to Use Avatars - **User identification**: Profile areas, user lists, comments sections, and author attribution - **Team representation**: Member lists, collaboration interfaces, and group displays - **Entity representation**: Organizations, projects, departments, or system accounts - **Navigation elements**: User menus, account switching, and profile access points - **Social features**: Comments, reviews, messaging, and activity feeds - **Contact lists**: Address books, directory listings, and people browsing ### When NOT to Use Avatars - **Decorative images**: Use Image component for non-representative visuals or illustrations - **Large portraits**: Use dedicated image

title: Badge
description: Badges highlight important information with small, prominent labels. They indicate status, counts, categories, or draw attention to specific content.
content: # Badge Badges are small visual labels that help users quickly understand status and categories. The ELEVATE Badge component helps designers and developers create consistent, accessible interfaces that communicate important information without overwhelming the user. ## Overview ### When to Use Badges - **Status indication**: Online/offline, active/inactive, approval states - **Categorization**: Tags, labels, content classification - **Metadata**: Version numbers, types, feature flags - **Highlighting**: Important or featured content that needs attention ### When NOT to Use Badges - **Primary actions**: Use Button component for main interactions - **Navigation**: Use Link or navigation components for page transitions - **Notification counts**: Use Indicator component for unread counts, new items, alerts - **Large text content**: Use appropriate text components for substantial information - **Complex information**: Use Cards or other layout components for detailed data ## Variations ###

title: Breadcrumb
description: Breadcrumbs show users their location within a site hierarchy and provide quick navigation to parent pages. They improve wayfinding and user orientation.
content: # Breadcrumb Breadcrumbs are navigational aids that show users their current location within a website's hierarchy and provide quick navigation to parent pages. The ELEVATE Breadcrumb component helps designers and developers create consistent wayfinding patterns that reduce cognitive load and improve user orientation in complex information architectures. ## Overview ### When to Use Breadcrumbs - **Deep hierarchies**: Sites with 3+ levels of navigation structure - **Complex information architecture**: Multiple categories and subcategories - **User orientation**: When users need to understand their current location - **Quick navigation**: Allowing fast access to parent levels without browser back button - **E-commerce sites**: Product categories and detailed product pages - **Documentation sites**: Multi-level content organization ### When NOT to Use Breadcrumbs - **Shallow sites**: Sites with only 1-2 navigation levels - **Linear workflows**: Step-by-step processes or wizards (use progr

title: Breadcrumb Item
description: Individual items within breadcrumb navigation that represent specific levels in the site hierarchy. They provide clickable links to parent pages.
content: Breadcrumb Items are the individual elements that make up breadcrumb navigation. The ELEVATE Breadcrumb Item component helps designers and developers create consistent styling and behavior for each level in the navigation hierarchy, supporting various states and interaction patterns that enhance wayfinding experiences. ## Overview ### When to Use Breadcrumb Items - **Hierarchical navigation**: Each level in a multi-tier site structure - **Page identification**: Showing the current location context within the hierarchy - **Quick navigation**: Providing shortcuts to parent levels without browser back button - **Path visualization**: Making site structure clear and understandable to users - **Context preservation**: Maintaining user orientation during deep navigation ### When NOT to Use Breadcrumb Items - **Single-level navigation**: Simple sites without hierarchical structure - **Linear processes**: Step-by-step workflows or wizards (use progress indicators) - **Primary navigation**: Mai

title: Button
description: Buttons trigger actions and guide users through workflows. They provide clear affordances and communicate hierarchy through visual styling.
content: # Button Buttons are the primary interface for user actions in digital products. The ELEVATE Button component helps designers and developers create consistent, accessible interfaces that guide users through workflows with clear visual hierarchy and meaningful interactions. ## Overview ### When to Use Buttons - **Primary actions**: Sign up, submit, save, confirm, purchase - **Secondary actions**: Cancel, back, learn more, edit - **Navigation**: Next step, continue, proceed to checkout - **Destructive actions**: Delete, remove, reset, archive ### When NOT to Use Buttons - **Links**: Use Link component for navigation between pages or external sites - **Toggles**: Use Switch component for on/off states or settings - **Selection**: Use Checkbox or Radio for multiple choice selections - **Filters**: Use FilterButton or Chip components for content filtering ## Variations ### Tone Each tone communicates a different type of action and creates visual hierarchy in your interface. ### Size ### Sta

title: Button Group
description: Button Groups organize related actions together with consistent spacing and visual treatment. They provide clear action hierarchy and improved user experience.
content: Button Groups combine multiple related buttons into a cohesive unit with consistent spacing, alignment, and visual treatment. The ELEVATE Button Group component helps designers and developers organize actions logically, create clear visual hierarchy, and reduce interface complexity while maintaining accessibility and usability standards. ## Overview ### When to Use Button Groups - **Related actions**: Buttons that perform similar or complementary functions - **Action sets**: Save/Cancel, Previous/Next, Accept/Decline pairs - **Toolbars**: Sets of tools or commands in applications - **Bulk actions**: Multiple operations that can be performed on selected content - **Workflow steps**: Sequential actions in a multi-step process - **Form actions**: Multiple submission or navigation options ### When NOT to Use Button Groups - **Unrelated actions**: Buttons that serve completely different purposes - **Primary navigation**: Use appropriate navigation components instead - **Single actions**: In

title: Card
description: Cards are flexible containers that group related content and actions. They provide visual hierarchy and structure to complex interfaces.
content: # Card Cards are versatile containers that organize related information and actions into digestible sections. The ELEVATE Card component helps designers and developers create consistent, accessible layouts that structure complex information clearly and support user workflows. ## Overview ### When to Use Cards - **Content grouping**: Related information that belongs together logically - **Data display**: Metrics, statistics, dashboards, or summary information - **Navigation**: Category links, feature highlights, landing page sections - **Product listings**: Items in catalogs, directories, or search results - **Information hierarchy**: Breaking complex content into digestible sections ### When NOT to Use Cards - **Simple lists**: Use List component for basic item collections - **Form sections**: Use proper form fieldsets or sections for form organization - **Full-page layouts**: Use appropriate layout components for main page structure - **Inline content**: Use appropriate text component

title: Charts (Planned)
description: Charts visualize data relationships and trends through various graphical representations. This component is currently in planning phase and not yet available in ELEVATE Core UI.
content: :::info Component Status: Planned The ELEVATE Charts component is currently in planning and development phase. This documentation demonstrates the intended patterns and functionality for future implementation. The examples shown use existing ELEVATE components combined with SVG and CSS to create chart interfaces. ::: Charts transform raw data into visual insights that users can quickly understand and act upon. The planned ELEVATE Charts component will help designers and developers create consistent, accessible data visualizations that communicate information clearly and support data-driven decision making. ## Overview ### When to Use Charts - **Data comparison**: Compare values across categories or time periods - **Trend visualization**: Show changes and patterns over time - **Part-to-whole relationships**: Display how individual parts make up a total - **Performance metrics**: Dashboard KPIs and business intelligence displays - **Progress tracking**: Show completion status and goal ac

title: Checkbox
description: Checkboxes allow users to select one or more options from a set. They provide clear visual feedback and support various states for form interactions.
content: # Checkbox Checkboxes are form controls that allow users to select one or multiple options from a list. The ELEVATE Checkbox component helps designers and developers create consistent, accessible selection interfaces that clearly communicate state and provide inclusive interaction patterns for all users. ## Overview ### When to Use Checkboxes - **Multiple selections**: When users can choose several options from a list - **Optional settings**: Features that can be enabled or disabled independently - **Agreement confirmations**: Terms, conditions, privacy policies, consent forms - **Filter controls**: Narrowing down search results or content views - **Bulk actions**: Selecting multiple items for operations like delete or export - **Preference settings**: User customization options that can be combined ### When NOT to Use Checkboxes - **Single selection**: Use Radio buttons for exclusive choices from a group - **Binary toggles**: Use Switch component for on/off states with immediate effec

title: Chip
description: Chips represent small pieces of information, selections, or actions. They provide compact ways to display attributes, tags, or interactive elements.
content: Chips are compact elements that help users manage selections, filters, and tags efficiently. The ELEVATE Chip component helps designers and developers create consistent, accessible interfaces for content organization and user interactions. ## Overview ### When to Use Chips - **Tags and labels**: Categorizing or labeling content for easy identification - **Active filters**: Showing applied search or content filters with remove options - **User selections**: Displaying chosen options from multi-select interactions - **Compact actions**: Space-constrained interactive elements for secondary actions - **Status indicators**: Quick status communication with dismissible options ### When NOT to Use Chips - **Primary actions**: Use Button component for main interactions users need to take - **Long text content**: Use appropriate text components for substantial information - **Complex information**: Use Card or other layout components for detailed data - **Navigation**: Use Link or navigation com

title: Date Picker
description: Date Picker allows users to select dates from a calendar interface or text input. It provides intuitive date selection with formatting, validation, and localization support.
content: # Date Picker Date Picker simplifies date selection for users while ensuring proper formatting and validation. The ELEVATE Date Picker component helps designers and developers create consistent, accessible date input experiences that work across different locales and use cases. ## Overview ### When to Use Date Picker - **Event scheduling**: Appointments, meetings, and calendar events - **Booking systems**: Travel, reservations, and service bookings - **Data filtering**: Date range filters for reports and analytics - **Form inputs**: Birth dates, deadlines, and important dates - **Time-sensitive content**: Publication dates and expiration times ### When NOT to Use Date Picker - **Approximate dates**: Use text input for "around 2020" or vague timeframes - **Historical dates**: Very old dates may be better as separate year/month inputs - **Time-only selection**: Use Time Picker component for time without dates - **Simple text**: When users prefer typing familiar formats like "tomorrow" ##

title: Dialog
description: Dialogs present important information or require user decisions. They overlay the main interface and focus attention on critical tasks or messages.
content: # Dialog Dialogs are modal windows that interrupt the user's workflow to present important information, gather input, or require decisions. The ELEVATE Dialog component provides accessible, responsive modal interactions for all INFORM applications. ## Overview ### When to Use Dialogs - **Critical decisions**: Destructive actions, important confirmations - **Required input**: Essential information needed to continue - **Error handling**: Critical errors that need immediate attention - **Complex forms**: Multi-step processes or detailed data entry - **Content preview**: Quick view of detailed information ### When NOT to Use Dialogs - **Simple notifications**: Use Toast or Notification components - **Non-critical information**: Use inline messaging or cards - **Primary navigation**: Use appropriate navigation patterns - **Frequent interactions**: Consider inline editing or side panels ## Variations ### Dialog Types Each dialog type serves a specific purpose and provides appropriate user e

title: Divider
description: Dividers create visual separation between content sections. They help organize information hierarchy and improve content scanability through subtle visual boundaries.
content: Dividers provide subtle visual separation that helps users understand content relationships and hierarchy. The ELEVATE Divider component helps designers and developers create consistent, accessible interfaces that organize information clearly without creating visual clutter. ## Overview ### When to Use Dividers - **Content sections**: Separate distinct topics or categories within a page - **List items**: Create visual breaks between related but separate list entries - **Form groups**: Organize form fields into logical sections - **Navigation menus**: Separate menu groups or categories - **Card content**: Divide different types of information within cards ### When NOT to Use Dividers - **White space is sufficient**: Don't add dividers when spacing already creates clear separation - **Overuse**: Too many dividers create visual noise and reduce their effectiveness - **Primary navigation**: Use proper navigation components instead of divider-separated links - **Data tables**: Use proper ta

title: Drawer
description: Drawers provide temporary overlay surfaces that slide in from screen edges. They offer additional content or navigation without leaving the current context.
content: Drawers expand interface real estate without navigating away from the current context. The ELEVATE Drawer component helps designers and developers create consistent, accessible overlay experiences that provide additional functionality while maintaining user focus and orientation. ## Overview ### When to Use Drawers - **Navigation menus**: Mobile-friendly navigation that doesn't take up screen space - **Filters and options**: Advanced filtering controls for search and data views - **Secondary actions**: Additional tools and options that support the main workflow - **Content details**: Expandable information panels without page navigation - **Settings panels**: Configuration options that apply to current context ### When NOT to Use Drawers - **Primary content**: Main content should not be hidden in drawers - **Critical actions**: Essential user actions should be immediately visible - **Small content**: Simple content that fits better in tooltips or popovers - **Multi-step processes**: Us

title: Dropdown
description: Dropdowns allow users to select from a list of options in a compact interface. They save screen space while providing access to multiple choices.
content: Dropdowns provide efficient option selection within constrained interface space. The ELEVATE Dropdown component helps designers and developers create consistent, accessible selection experiences that work well across different contexts and device types. ## Overview ### When to Use Dropdowns - **Form selections**: Country, state, category, and type selections - **Filters and sorting**: Data table filters and sort options - **Settings menus**: Configuration options and preferences - **Action menus**: Context-specific actions and commands - **Navigation**: Secondary navigation and menu structures ### When NOT to Use Dropdowns - **Two options**: Use radio buttons or toggle switches for binary choices - **Many options**: Consider autocomplete or search for 10+ options - **Always visible info**: Use visible text for frequently referenced information - **Primary navigation**: Use dedicated navigation components for main site sections ## Variations ### Basic Dropdown Standard dropdown for sele

title: Empty State
description: Placeholder component for when no content or data is available, providing helpful guidance and next steps to users
content: # Empty State Empty State components provide helpful placeholders when no content, data, or search results are available. They guide users with clear messaging and actionable next steps to improve the user experience during empty scenarios. ## When to Use - **No Data**: When lists, tables, or data views have no items - **Search Results**: When search queries return no matches - **First Time Use**: When users haven't created content yet - **Error Recovery**: After failed operations that result in empty states ## Basic Usage ## Search Results ## First Time Experience ## Properties | Property | Type | Default | Description | |----------|------|---------|-------------| | `icon` | `string` | | Icon name from ELEVATE icon library | | `title` | `string` | | Main heading text | | `description` | `string` | | Descriptive text explaining the empty state | | `action-text` | `string` | | Text for the primary action button | | `action-href` | `string` | | URL for the action button (makes it a link)

title: Expansion Panel
description: Collapsible content sections that allow users to show and hide detailed information with smooth animations
content: # Expansion Panel Expansion Panels provide collapsible content sections that help organize and manage information density. They allow users to show and hide detailed content on demand, making interfaces more scannable and less overwhelming. ## When to Use - **Content Organization**: Group related information into expandable sections - **Progressive Disclosure**: Show summary first, details on demand - **Space Conservation**: Reduce visual clutter in dense interfaces - **FAQ Sections**: Organize frequently asked questions and answers ## Basic Usage ## With Icon and Description ## Multiple Panels ## Properties | Property | Type | Default | Description | |----------|------|---------|-------------| | `expanded` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the panel is expanded by default | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction with the panel | | `icon` | `string` | | Icon name to display in the header | | `variant` | `'default' \| 'bordered' \| 'elevated'` | `'default'` | Visual sty

title: Expansion Panel Group
description: Container component for managing multiple expansion panels with coordinated behavior and consistent styling
content: # Expansion Panel Group Expansion Panel Group provides a container for multiple expansion panels with coordinated behavior, consistent styling, and advanced features like accordion mode where only one panel can be expanded at a time. ## When to Use - **Settings Pages**: Group related configuration sections - **FAQ Sections**: Organize questions and answers with accordion behavior - **Multi-Step Forms**: Break complex forms into manageable sections - **Content Organization**: Structure dense information into collapsible sections ## Basic Usage ## Accordion Mode ## Bordered Variant ## Properties | Property | Type | Default | Description | |----------|------|---------|-------------| | `accordion` | `boolean` | `false` | Enable accordion mode (only one panel expanded) | | `variant` | `'default' \| 'bordered' \| 'elevated'` | `'default'` | Visual style variant | | `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | Overall size of panels in the group | | `gap` | `'none' \| 'small' \| '

title: Field
description: Form field wrapper component that provides consistent labeling, validation, help text, and error handling for form inputs
content: # Field Field is a wrapper component that provides consistent labeling, validation states, help text, and error handling for form inputs. It ensures all form fields follow ELEVATE design patterns and accessibility standards. ## When to Use - **Form Consistency**: Standardize all form field layouts and styling - **Validation Display**: Show validation states and error messages - **Accessibility**: Ensure proper labeling and ARIA attributes - **Help Text**: Provide additional context and guidance ## Basic Usage ## Resources - **[Form Guidelines](/docs/patterns/data-entry-forms)** - Best practices for form design - **[Accessibility](/docs/guidelines/accessibility)** - Form accessibility standards - **[Storybook](https://elevate-core-ui.inform-cloud.io/?path=/docs/components-field)** - Interactive examples and API documentation --- :::tip Consistent Validation Use the Field component consistently across your application to ensure all form fields have the same validation styling and behavio

title: File Dropzone
description: Drag and drop file upload component with support for multiple files, file type validation, and upload progress feedback
content: # File Dropzone File Dropzone provides an intuitive drag-and-drop interface for file uploads, supporting multiple files, file type validation, and visual feedback during the upload process. ## Resources - **[Button](/docs/components/button)** - Upload action buttons - **[Progress](/docs/components/progress)** - Upload progress indicators - **[Storybook](https://elevate-core-ui.inform-cloud.io/?path=/docs/components-file-dropzone)** - Interactive examples and API documentation ## Changelog

title: Icon
description: Icons provide visual communication through recognizable symbols. They enhance usability by communicating concepts quickly and supporting text-based information.
content: # Icon Icons create visual consistency and improve interface comprehension through universal symbols. The ELEVATE Icon component helps designers and developers create consistent, accessible interfaces that communicate effectively across language and cultural barriers. ## Overview ### When to Use Icons - **Action identification**: Buttons, menu items, and interactive elements - **Status indication**: Success, warning, error, and information states - **Navigation aids**: Wayfinding and section identification - **Content categorization**: Document types, content themes, and classifications - **Visual reinforcement**: Supporting text with recognizable symbols ### When NOT to Use Icons - **Unclear concepts**: Avoid icons for abstract or ambiguous ideas - **Cultural specificity**: Don't use icons that may not translate across cultures - **Decoration only**: Icons should serve functional purposes, not just visual appeal - **Overcrowding**: Too many icons create visual noise and reduce effecti

title: Overview
description: Interactive UI components built with the ELEVATE Design System. Each component is designed for accessibility, consistency, and ease of use.
content: # Components overview Explore the complete collection of ELEVATE UI components. Each component is designed with accessibility, consistency, and developer experience in mind.

title: Indicator
description: Indicators attach notification counts, alerts, or status dots to other components. They show overlay information like unread messages, new items, or status states.
content: # Indicator Indicators are small notification overlays that attach to other components to show counts, alerts, or status information. The ELEVATE Indicator component helps create accessible, attention-grabbing notifications without overwhelming the interface. ## Overview ### When to Use Indicators - **Notification counts**: Unread messages, new items, pending tasks - **Status alerts**: Error states, warnings, success confirmations - **Activity indicators**: Online status, active processes, live updates - **Attention signals**: New features, important updates, required actions ### When NOT to Use Indicators - **Primary content**: Use Badge component for main labels and status - **Navigation**: Use dedicated navigation indicators or breadcrumbs - **Large amounts of text**: Use appropriate text components for substantial information - **Decorative purposes**: Indicators should always convey meaningful information ## Variations ### Count Indicators Indicators displaying numeric values usin

title: Input
description: Input fields allow users to enter and edit text. They provide clear affordances for data entry with validation feedback and accessibility features.
content: # Input Input components are essential form elements that allow users to enter text, numbers, and other data. The ELEVATE Input component provides consistent styling, validation states, and accessibility features across all INFORM applications. ## Overview ### When to Use Inputs - **Data entry**: Text, numbers, emails, passwords, and other user input - **Search functionality**: Search boxes and filtering interfaces - **Forms**: Registration, contact forms, settings, and configuration - **Content creation**: Comments, posts, descriptions, and text content ### When NOT to Use Inputs - **Binary choices**: Use Switch or Checkbox for yes/no selections - **Multiple selections**: Use Select, Dropdown, or Checkbox group for multiple options - **Large text**: Use Textarea component for multi-line text input - **Dates**: Use DatePicker for date selection with calendar interface ## Variations ### Input Types Different input types provide specific keyboard layouts and validation on mobile devices.

title: Lightbox
description: Media viewing overlay component that displays images, videos, and other content in a modal interface with zoom and navigation controls
content: # Lightbox Lightbox provides an overlay interface for viewing media content like images and videos in a focused, modal environment with zoom controls, navigation, and keyboard support. ## When to Use - **Image Galleries**: View images in full size with navigation - **Media Preview**: Preview videos, documents, or other media - **Product Images**: Detailed product image viewing in e-commerce - **Portfolio Display**: Showcase design work or photography ## Basic Usage ## Resources - **[Dialog](/docs/components/dialog)** - Modal component for general overlay content - **[Button](/docs/components/button)** - Navigation and control buttons in lightbox - **[Storybook](https://elevate-core-ui.inform-cloud.io/?path=/docs/components-lightbox)** - Interactive examples and API documentation ## Changelog

title: Link
description: Navigation component for internal and external links with consistent styling and accessibility support
content: # Link Link component provides consistent styling and accessibility features for navigation elements, supporting both internal navigation and external links with proper semantic markup. ## Resources - **[Button](/docs/components/button)** - Button component for actions vs navigation - **[Breadcrumb](/docs/components/breadcrumb)** - Breadcrumb navigation links - **[Storybook](https://elevate-core-ui.inform-cloud.io/?path=/docs/components-link)** - Interactive examples and API documentation ::: ## Changelog

title: Menu
description: Navigation menu component for organizing menu items with hierarchical structure and keyboard navigation support
content: # Menu Menu component provides structured navigation with support for menu items, separators, and hierarchical organization. It includes full keyboard navigation and accessibility features. ## Resources - **[Menu Item](/docs/components/menu-item)** - Individual items within menus - **[Breadcrumb](/docs/components/breadcrumb)** - Alternative navigation pattern - **[Storybook](https://elevate-core-ui.inform-cloud.io/?path=/docs/components-menu)** - Interactive examples and API documentation ::: ## Changelog

title: Menu Item
description: Individual menu item component with support for icons, labels, shortcuts, and various interaction states
content: # Menu Item Menu Item represents individual items within menus, supporting icons, labels, keyboard shortcuts, and various states like active, disabled, and selected. ## Resources - **[Menu](/docs/components/menu)** - Container component for menu items - **[Button](/docs/components/button)** - Alternative action component - **[Storybook](https://elevate-core-ui.inform-cloud.io/?path=/docs/components-menu-item)** - Interactive examples and API documentation ::: ## Changelog

title: Mutation Observer
description: Utility component that observes DOM changes and provides reactive behavior for dynamic content and element modifications.
content: # Mutation Observer The Mutation Observer component provides a declarative way to observe DOM changes and react to modifications in the document structure, attributes, or content. ## Usage Guidelines ### When to Use - **Dynamic content monitoring** - Watching for content changes in dynamic applications - **Attribute tracking** - Observing attribute changes on elements - **DOM structure monitoring** - Detecting when elements are added or removed - **Reactive components** - Building components that respond to external changes - **Accessibility updates** - Tracking changes that affect assistive technologies ### When Not to Use - **Simple event handling** - Use standard event listeners for user interactions - **Performance-critical operations** - Heavy DOM observation can impact performance - **Static content** - Unnecessary for content that doesn't change after initial render ## Basic Usage This content will be observed for changes Add Content function addContent() { const container = doc

title: Notification
description: System message component for displaying alerts, confirmations, errors, and informational messages to users
content: # Notification Notification component displays system messages, alerts, and feedback to users with different severity levels and optional actions. ## Resources - **[Badge](/docs/components/badge)** - Status indicators and counts - **[Button](/docs/components/button)** - Action buttons in notifications - **[Storybook](https://elevate-core-ui.inform-cloud.io/?path=/docs/components-notification)** - Interactive examples and API documentation ::: ## Changelog

title: Paginator
description: Navigation component for breaking large datasets into manageable pages with controls for navigation and page size selection
content: # Paginator Paginator provides navigation controls for large datasets, allowing users to navigate between pages and optionally control page size. ## Resources - **[Button](/docs/components/button)** - Navigation buttons in pagination - **[Select](/docs/components/select)** - Page size selection dropdown - **[Storybook](https://elevate-core-ui.inform-cloud.io/?path=/docs/components-paginator)** - Interactive examples and API documentation ::: ## Changelog

title: Popup
description: A popup component that displays content in a floating panel, typically used for tooltips, dropdown menus, or contextual information.
content: # Popup The Popup component provides a flexible way to display content in a floating panel that appears relative to a trigger element. It's commonly used for tooltips, dropdown menus, contextual information, or small forms that need to appear over existing content. ## Overview ### When to Use Popup - **Tooltips**: Additional information or help text - **Dropdown menus**: Actions or navigation options - **Contextual information**: Details that don't warrant a full page - **Quick forms**: Small input forms or settings panels - **Preview content**: Quick preview of larger content ### When NOT to Use Popup - **Major workflows**: Use Dialog or dedicated pages for complex tasks - **Critical information**: Use notifications for important system messages - **Large content**: Use dedicated pages for substantial content - **Mobile primary actions**: Consider full-screen alternatives on mobile ## Status :::warning Development Status This component was recently added in version 0.0.28-alpha and ma

title: Progress
description: Visual indicator component for showing task completion status with determinate and indeterminate states
content: # Progress Progress component provides visual feedback for task completion, file uploads, form submission, and other processes with determinate and indeterminate states. ## Resources - **[Badge](/docs/components/badge)** - Status indicators and labels - **[Button](/docs/components/button)** - Cancel or pause actions for progress - **[Storybook](https://elevate-core-ui.inform-cloud.io/?path=/docs/components-progress)** - Interactive examples and API documentation ::: ## Changelog

title: Radio
description: Radio components allow users to select one option from a set of mutually exclusive choices. The ELEVATE Radio component provides accessible single-selection functionality with consistent styling.
content: # Radio Radio buttons enable users to select exactly one option from a group of mutually exclusive choices. The ELEVATE Radio component ensures accessible, consistent single-selection interfaces that integrate seamlessly with forms and the design system. ## Overview ### When to Use Radio Buttons - **Mutually exclusive choices**: When users must select exactly one option from a group - **Preference settings**: Setting default options or user preferences - **Configuration options**: Choosing between different configuration modes - **Survey responses**: Single-answer survey questions and forms - **Payment methods**: Selecting one payment option from available choices ### When NOT to Use Radio Buttons - **Multiple selections**: Use checkboxes when users can select multiple options - **Binary choices**: Use switches or single checkboxes for simple on/off choices - **Many options**: Consider dropdowns or other components for large option sets - **Optional selection**: When no selection is a

title: Radio Group
description: Radio group component that manages multiple radio buttons as a cohesive group with shared validation and accessibility features.
content: # Radio Group Radio groups organize multiple radio buttons into a logical group, ensuring only one option can be selected at a time while providing consistent validation and accessibility features. ## Usage Guidelines ### When to Use - **Mutually exclusive choices** - When users need to select exactly one option from a list - **Form organization** - To group related radio buttons with shared validation - **Accessibility** - When you need proper keyboard navigation and screen reader support - **Validation** - When the group requires collective validation or error messaging ### When Not to Use - **Multiple selections** - Use checkbox groups instead - **Single options** - Use individual checkboxes for standalone choices - **Large option lists** - Consider select dropdowns for 7+ options ## Basic Usage Email Phone Mail `} > Email Phone Mail ## Component API ### Properties | Property | Type | Default | Description | |----------|------|---------|-------------| | `label` | `string` | - | Acce

title: Resize Observer
description: Utility component that observes element size changes and provides reactive behavior for responsive layouts and dynamic sizing.
content: # Resize Observer The Resize Observer component provides a declarative way to observe element size changes and react to dimension modifications, enabling responsive behavior and dynamic layouts. ## Usage Guidelines ### When to Use - **Responsive components** - Building components that adapt to container size changes - **Dynamic layouts** - Creating layouts that respond to content or viewport changes - **Performance optimization** - Optimizing rendering based on available space - **Container queries** - Implementing container-based responsive design - **Chart and visualization** - Updating graphics when containers resize ### When Not to Use - **Viewport changes only** - Use media queries for viewport-based responsive design - **Static layouts** - Unnecessary for fixed-size content - **Performance-critical code** - Frequent resize observations can impact performance ## Basic Usage Resize this box by dragging the corner Size will be displayed here document.addEventListener('elvt-resize',

title: Select
description: Select components allow users to choose from a list of options. They save space while providing clear choices and supporting search functionality for larger option sets.
content: # Select Select components provide efficient option selection through dropdown interfaces that save screen space while offering clear choices. description: Comprehensive accessibility guidelines ensuring inclusive experiences for all users with WCAG 2.1 AA compliance

title: Themes
description: Learn how to implement and customize themes in ELEVATE Design System
content: # Themes ELEVATE Design System includes comprehensive theming support, allowing you to create consistent visual experiences across light and dark modes, as well as custom brand themes. ## Built-in Themes ### Light Theme (Default) The light theme provides optimal readability in bright environments with light backgrounds and dark text. **Characteristics:** - Light backgrounds (#ffffff, #f8fafc) - Dark text for optimal contrast - Subtle shadows for depth - Blue primary color (#0072ff) ### Dark Theme The dark theme reduces eye strain in low-light environments with dark backgrounds and light text. **Characteristics:** - Dark backgrounds (#1a1a1a, #2d2d2d) - Light text for readability - Enhanced shadows for depth - Brighter accent colors ## Theme Implementation ### Automatic Theme Switching Implement automatic theme switching based on user's system preference: ### Manual Theme Toggle Allow users to manually switch between themes: ### CSS Implementation ## Custom Themes ### Brand Theme Creati

title: Application Shell
description: Enterprise application shell pattern with module switcher and navigation for ELEVATE applications
content: # Application Shell Pattern The Application Shell pattern provides a consistent layout structure for enterprise applications, featuring integrated module switching and hierarchical navigation. This pattern is essential for multi-module applications where users need to switch between different functional areas while maintaining context and navigation state. ## Pattern Overview The application shell serves as the foundational layout that wraps all application content, providing: - **Global Navigation Header** - Top-level branding, user controls, and system-wide actions - **Module Switcher** - Switch between different application modules or products - **Module Menu** - Context-sensitive navigation within the current module - **Main Content Area** - Dynamic content based on current route and module - **Footer** (optional) - Additional links, legal information, or system status ## When to Use Use the application shell pattern when: - Building multi-module enterprise applications - Users nee

title: Design Patterns
description: Common UI patterns, templates, and interaction designs for building consistent user experiences with ELEVATE
content: # Design Patterns Design patterns provide proven solutions to common user interface challenges. These patterns help teams build consistent, predictable, and effective user experiences across all INFORM products and applications. ## What Are Design Patterns? Design patterns are reusable solutions to recurring design problems. They represent best practices for organizing information, structuring interactions, and creating intuitive user experiences. **Benefits of Using Patterns:** - 🔄 **Consistency** - Unified experience across products - ⚡ **Efficiency** - Faster design and development - 🎯 **Usability** - Proven interaction models - 🛡️ **Reliability** - Tested and validated solutions - 📚 **Knowledge Sharing** - Common vocabulary and understanding ## Pattern Categories ### Navigation Patterns **[Primary Navigation](/docs/patterns/primary-navigation)** Core navigation structures for applications and websites. **[Breadcrumbs](/docs/patterns/breadcrumbs)** Secondary navigation showing u
